uncited: Memory Layout Optimization encompasses techniques for arranging volumetric data in contiguous memory buffers to maximize spatial locality, minimize cache misses, and eliminate hardware memory bank conflicts during rendering.
It solves the problem where naive linear indexing causes cache thrashing or SDRAM bank conflicts, leading to performance degradation.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Evaluation Cache](874-evaluation-cache.md) (which caches computed values) and [Tile-based Volume Ray Marching](1678-tile-based-volume-ray-marching.md) (which optimizes traversal order) by focusing exclusively on the physical storage arrangement of the voxel data itself.
Register-form kernels read every shell of a chunk from groupshared memory: centre, cutoff, $l$, AO count, primitives, and rows of $C$.
Inner loop no longer waits on dependent global loads per shell.
Memory layout optimization techniques originated from the need to overcome CPU cache hierarchy limitations and early GPU memory controller constraints.

Out-of-core techniques like [Memory-Insensitive Rendering](2774-memory-insensitive-rendering.md) were introduced to handle datasets exceeding available RAM by bypassing memory bottlenecks via external sorting.
